------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The body of each wage determination lists the classifications and wage rates that have been found to be prevailing for the type(s) of construction and geographic area covered by the wage determination. The classifications are listed in alphabetical order under rate identifiers indicating whether the particular rate is a union rate (current union negotiated rate), a survey rate, a weighted union average rate, a state adopted rate, or a supplemental classification rate. Union Rate Identifiers A four-letter identifier beginning with characters other than � SU � , � UAVG � , � SA � , or � SC � denotes that a union rate was prevailing for that classification in the survey. Example: PLUM0198-005 07/01/2024. PLUM is an identifier of the union whose collectively bargained rate prevailed in the survey for this classification, which in this example would be Plumbers. 0198 indicates the local union number or district council number where applicable, i.e., Plumbers Local 0198. The next number, 005 in the example, is an internal number used in processing the wage determination. The date, 07/01/2024 in the example, is the effective date of the most current negotiated rate. e collectively bargained rate prevailed in the survey for this classification, which in this example would be Plumbers. 0198 indicates the local union number or district council number where applicable, i.e., Plumbers Local 0198. The next number, 005 in the example, is an internal number used in processing the wage determination. The date, 07/01/2024 in the example, is the effective date of the most current negotiated rate. Union prevailing wage rates are updated to reflect all changes over time that are reported to WHD in the rates in the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) governing the classification. Union Average Rate Identifiers The UAVG identifier indicates that no single rate prevailed for those classifications, but that 100% of the data reported for the classifications reflected union rates. EXAMPLE: UAVG-OH-0010 01/01/2024. UAVG indicates that the rate is a weighted union average rate. OH indicates the State of Ohio. The next number, 0010 in the example, is an internal number used in producing the wage determination. The date, 01/01/2024 in the example, indicates the date the wage determination was updated to reflect the most current union average rate. PLANXS was competitively awarded in September 2021 through a small business set aside solicitation under the Chief Information Officer—Solutions and Partners 3 (CIO-SP3) Small Business (SB) Government-Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC). This work is currently being completed under the PLANXS task order. The services will maintain interoperability by enabling a data hub which integrates and shares seamlessly. The contractor will use advanced analytical tools to support interactive decision making, continuous monitoring and improvement of predictive machine learning

MARCORLOGCOM’s Workforce-21 initiative is a proactive workforce development strategy designed to sustain a highly capable, agile workforce prepared to operate within a dynamic and digitally connected logistics environment. To support the professional growth of its personnel within the Logistics Community of Interest (COI) occupational series (0346, 2010, 2003, 2005), MARCORLOGCOM requires a comprehensive training program. sla_onsite.text: undamentals and Supply Chain Management Training 1.0 BACKGROUND The Marine Corps Logistics Command (MARCORLOGCOM) mission is to provide worldwide, integrated logistics, supply chain, and distribution management; depot-level maintenance management; and strategic pre-positioning capability in support of the operating forces and other supported units. This support maximizes organizational readiness and sustainability, while driving enterprise and program-level Total Life Cycle Management. MARCORLOGCOM is comprised of three subordinate commands: • Marine Depot Maintenance Command (MDMC) • Marine Force Storage Command (MFSC) • Blount Island Command (BIC) Additionally, it consists of two dedicated centers: • Command Data Analytics Office • Weapons System Management Center Each of these organizations has a direct, critical role in supporting and executing the Command’s primary mission. MARCORLOGCOM’s Workforce-21 initiative is a proactive workforce development strategy designed to sustain a highly capable, agile workforce prepared to operate within a dynamic and digitally connected logistics environment. To support the professional growth of its personnel within the Logistics Community of Interest (COI) occupational series (0346, 2010, 2003, 2005), MARCORLOGCOM require

gitally connected logistics environment. To support the professional growth of its personnel within the Logistics Community of Interest (COI) occupational series (0346, 2010, 2003, 2005), MARCORLOGCOM requires a comprehensive training program. This program will enable up to twenty-five (25) individuals to obtain professional certificates across two structured tracks: a Logistics Fundamentals Certificate Program (Entry-Level) and a subsequent Supply Chain Management Certificate Program (Journeyman-Level). 2.0 SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT The Contractor shall provide all qualified personnel, labor, instructional materials, coordination, and travel necessary to deliver a one-time facilitation of six (6) professional training courses for a single cohort of up to twenty-five (25) participants. The Contractor shall develop their own curriculum consistent with the course descriptions. The program is structured as follows: • Four (4) Logistics Fundamentals (Entry-Level) Courses • Two (2) Supply Chain Management (Journeyman-Level) Courses 2.1 Delivery Structure and Duration • Course Duration: To maximize knowledge retention and allow students to apply concepts in real-time, each course shall be three (3) days in duration. The overall program will span six (6) consecutive months. 3

General Information and Requirements Description of Work Specifications and Limitations: The purpose of this statement of work is to secure the service of mechanical mowing of approximately 2,878 acres of brush and grass from September 15, 2026 – January 15, 2027, in Humboldt County, Nevada. The areas are on the attached maps, with the location depicted to be mowed. This project is necessary for proactive fire mitigation in this high-risk wildfire area and will be completed through the removal of hazardous fuels along the roadside. This project is necessary for proactive fire mitigation in this high-risk wildfire area and will be completed through the removal of hazardous fuels along the roadside. Each line item will be bid and awarded separately, this may be to the same vendor or different vendors (see Bid Sheet). The Contractor will be responsible for furnishing all labor, equipment, supervision, transportation, supplies, and materials required to mechanically mow brush and grass within the project area(s) and within the specified performance time. The Contractor shall service and maintain such equipment as necessary to maintain satisfactory progress of work. Work Specifications: Fuel breaks will be mowed in the proposed footprint as mapped, in a linear fashion off one or both sides of the road. Mowing will be done on shrubs and/or perennial or annual grasses. Vegetation will be cut to a height of 4 to 6 inches in designated mowing areas except where rocks and terrain restrict access with equipment. Implementation will desist in the event wet conditions arise and there is excessive ground moisture. This occurs when the ground is saturated where equipment is causing excessive rutting (>3 inches) and disturbance. When saturated ground conditions are encountered, the Contractor shall stop work and notify the Contracti

The re-staking of mining claim markers would occur in coordination with the existing mining claimants to ensure accurate, legal staking procedures that would minimize damage to claims. All Contract equipment will be inspected by the BLM representative prior to equipment being offloaded from its transport. The inspection location needs to be pre-arranged with the Contracting Officer’s Representative to best serve both Contractor and BLM representative(s). Treatment areas are generally flat with some rolling hills. Treatment areas generally will consist of slopes less than 5%. Some rock is present and may need to be avoided by mowing equipment to prevent damage. Vegetation in the project area is typical of the Great Basin and consists of primarily sagebrush, other shrubs, and some grasses and forbs. Shrub and grass density varies throughout the treatment area. The nearest full support community to the project is Winnemucca, Nevada. Average travel time from Winnemucca to the project area is approximately 2.5 hours. The community of Paradise Valley, Nevada is closer to the project site with recreational hookup campgrounds and 1 multi fuel station 1.5 hours away. The project site may be reached by two-wheel drive vehicles when the main roads are dry, however access to the project area can be limited during the fall - winter months depending on weather. A high clearance 4 -wheel drive vehicle and UTV are highly recommended for access to project area sites, as road conditions include grown-in vegetation and rocky and uneven tracks. Prototype and integration of new capabilities and/or solutions addressing diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortages (DMSMS) are potential requirements that may be included in the effort. award_criteria.text: 2026Q0027_Warehouse_Welcome_Kits_2026.pdf ===== U.S. Embassy Canberra Date: 3rd August 2026 Dear Prospective Quoter: Subject: Request for Quotations number 19AS2026Q0027 Enclosed is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) for Supply and Delivery of Pre -Boxed Lodging Kits. If you would like to submit quotation, follow the instructions in Section 3 of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit it to the address shown on the Standard Form 1449 that follows this letter. The U.S. Government intends to award a purchase order to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer at the lowest price. We intend to award a purchase order based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. The Embassy intends to conduct a pre-quotation conference, online viewing only to be held on August 13 th, 2026, at 10:30am AEST. Prospective offerors/quoters should contact CNBGSOProcurement@state.gov by August 10th, 2026, at 4:00PM AEST for additional information. Quotations are due at 3pm AEST September 21st, 2026. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Proposals must be in English and incomplete proposals will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to cnbgsoprocurement@state.gov It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS -Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed the 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. In order for a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: 1. SF-14
